statement: Partition-key ordering closes the final hostile split/merge consumer gaps without new guardrail debt: every non-absent merge table ID is validated as a primitive string before absent ordering; evaluation partition arrays are consumed from own array data properties without iterator semantics and sorted through an Array.prototype.sort intrinsic captured at module load; compareRoutingKeys preserves all v6 routing semantics while returning below the complexity ratchet; and all v6/v5 SQLite-BINARY, numeric/TEXT, typed refusal, own-data metadata, prototype-pollution and consumer-ownership behavior remains unchanged.

constraints.statement: Supersedes sealed partition-key-ordering-owner-completion-v6 after exact-head Copilot review PR #88 rejected v6 for absent-peer table-ID validation, live array iterator/sort dependence in the actual merge path, and a new compareRoutingKeys complexity-ratchet violation. Preserve v6 predicate and evidence unchanged.

For merge evaluation table IDs, null/undefined may remain absent sentinels, but every non-absent peer is validated as a primitive string before any absent-order result can return. Invalid values fail closed in both operand directions without coercion.

The split/merge evaluation partition list is consumed from own array data properties only. A hostile own Symbol.iterator, inherited indices, accessors or holes cannot replace or synthesize partition rows.
Replacing Array.prototype.sort after module load cannot change or disable merge adjacency ordering; the sort intrinsic used by the owner is captured before hostile mutation.

The A1 candidate introduces no complexity-ratchet debt. compareRoutingKeys stays behaviorally identical to v6 while validation is factored below the repository threshold rather than waived or baselined.

Preserve invalid-versus-absent routing refusal, canonical finite -1/0/1 comparator results, SQLite BINARY UTF-8 including non-BMP, numeric/TEXT compatibility, same-reference invalid refusal, own-data iterator-free split metadata, own-data coercion-free table IDs including falsey values, prototype-pollution defenses, captured intrinsics and actual KeyRange/PartitionResolver/QueryGroup/split-merge owner expressions.

Table-ID invalid-versus-absent and partition-list iterator/sort witnesses must fail for the exact rejected v6 mechanism and pass only after the v7 repair; combined controls do not substitute for isolated witnesses where isolation is practical.
Persisted key type metadata, exact large-integer boundary representation, parser/bind precision, encoding migration and old-boundary revalidation remain A2.
Any v7 src/ candidate requires category-complete independent verification newer than its last attempt, covering both sealed verificationTemplates and exact candidate fingerprints.
No Raft runtime, consensus transport, lifecycle, membership or formation behavior changes.

The invalid-table-ID witness distinguishes all three supported absent shapes — missing property, own null and own undefined — in both operand directions; none may bypass primitive-string validation of the non-absent peer.

Partition IDs and partition start/end keys used by the live split/merge evaluator come only from own data properties with snake/camel fallback. Inherited values and accessors are not evaluation, sorting or adjacency authority and are never invoked.
